perspective:
Ethan Mohamud’s available information:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a Black man, a plumber, and a long-time close friend of Gary Guo since middle school. He knows Gary is a doctor.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation. Gary initially said he couldn’t because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks, delegating some responsibilities, and organizing Gary’s schedule so Gary could make time for himself. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. He saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and told Gary he was proud of him and available to talk.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that he was not as overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing better on his own with a healthier balance. Ethan felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always just a call away if needed.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control now.
